After years of scribbling notes into private notebooks and Jupyter cells, I decided it was
time to write in public.

## Who I am

I'm a financial engineer at PSP Investments in Montreal. My day-to-day involves quantitative
modelling in credit risk and derivatives — building tools that help understand complex financial
exposures across a large institutional portfolio.

Outside the office, I've been steadily building skills in machine learning and modern data
science, completing certifications in deep learning, TensorFlow, and Python data science.
I've also started experimenting with Julia, which I'm genuinely excited about for
numerical computing.

## What I'll write about

A mix of things:

- **Quantitative finance** — yield curves, derivatives pricing, counterparty credit risk
- **QuantLib** — practical guides to using QuantLib in Python
- **Machine learning in finance** — applying ML to financial problems
- **Julia** — numerical computing experiments
- **Tools and workflow** — how I set up and run my development environment

Some posts will be regular markdown. Others will be Jupyter notebooks rendered directly —
so you'll see live code output alongside the writing.

## Why public?

Writing forces clarity. And if even one post saves someone three hours of debugging a
QuantLib discount curve, it's worth the effort.

More soon.
